[list] | Slowly the gears of an old nation's war box began to turn and it all started with a simple audit of every single piece of military equipment, although one thing was desperately missing, intermediate missiles after all what good is a nation to do to strike from afar without a stockpile of rockets to do so?, and thus silently started the Ascoiyan Rocket Battalion, and soon enough the nation would go shopping for any vendor able to fit it's needs. | [/list][/quote]

Wuloosya's State Department and several defense contractors catch wind of Ascoiya's predicament. President Julian, influenced by the defense contractors' wishes to begin importing Wuloosyan weapons abroad for more cash flow, orders the State Department and War Department to begin formulating an offer to the country. The War Department is willing to transfer 5 of its Quasartico M30 HGVLs to the country, as Quasartico was already planning 10 more deliveries for the army later this year, and thus, the temporary loss of these systems wouldn't be devastating. The WDF can, however, offer, in far greater numbers, ATACMS Missiles, around a hundred that the army had been stockpiling, along with the 20 Quasartico M2AMS required to launch the system, and around 300 medium-range ballistic missiles and their accompanying launchers. These missiles had a range of around 2,000 km and were relatively cheap to produce. They had proved to be of great effectiveness during the war with Rosenmarkkee. To sweeten the deal, a guarantee of discounted reloads for the systems in the future would be made. In return, Wuloosya requested semiconductors from Acoysia to supplement future military and infrastructure development plans. Along with investments in the Ascoiyan economy to be held by the National Bank of Wuloosya. Once formulated, the offer would be sent through the Wuloosyan Embassy in Vespurias.

[spoiler=[b][pre]THE SILENT REAPER[/pre][/b] [i]Dont f*ck with H2S.[/i]]

Toju wiped sweat from his forehead with the back of his glove and leaned over the railing, heaving hard after just puking his lunch. The waves were battering the side of the massive rig, and he still wasnt used to offshore rig duty. He watched as the sea slapped the rig supports below, trying to hold back throwing up again.

Hey fleabag, an antagonizing voice beckoned from somewhere behind him. Theres some more catnip in the chow hall!

He looked back quickly, just in time to see two roughnecks walking off snickering to each other. The crew of the rig still wasnt used to working alongside a nonhuman. To be fair, nonhumans dont usually work on Seogyunese rigs; they dont even work on the mainland refineries. There isnt much that he can do about it though, because just as the roughnecks walked off, the zone supervisor locked eyes with Toju.

Did you ever shut off the number two valve? The supervisor, questioned, not even acknowledging Tojus slight green complexion.

Toju shook his head. I tried but I got sick before I could shut it off all the way. 

You better go finish the job. Were almost a month behind schedule and 

Toju just tuned him out. Every hour it was something about the whole rig behind schedule. He just nodded and went back to work. He walked down the narrow hallway, made a right and slid down the ladder. His tools stayed in the same place he dropped them at; a simple slugger wrench and a heavy hammer.

Toju picked the tools up and got back to work, using the wrench and hammer to close the valve. As he swung, he felt like something was off, but he didnt think about it for too long.

He blinked, then he let the hammer drop to his side. He was panting, almost as if he was about to be sick again. Thats when Toju smelt it, almost unmistakable.

Rotten eggs.

As soon as the smell hit his nose, it disappeared again. He shook his head. [i]Strange,[/i] he thought, then got back to swinging.

All of a sudden, Tojus vision blurred. He was so dizzy he couldnt focus. He dropped the hammer on the steel floor. [i]This cant be good.[/i]

The alarm on his vest began blaring, rattling Tojus already pounding head. Above deck, he heard other grunts running panicked.

Gas leak! He heard one of them shout. H2S!

Toju had no clue what that meant. He was never trained for a situation like this, but whatever it was, it was bad. He stumbled to the ladder, barely able to hold himself to it. He looked up, seeing shadows of men run past. Help, he rasped, barely able to hear his own voice.

A man with a gas mask happened to stop and look down the ladder. I got one down here! Someone help me get him up!

Before he knew it, Toju was hauled up the ladder and being laid on the floor. Get a f*ckin mask on him, now! He heard the supervisor from earlier bark out the order. A mask was placed down on his face.

Breathe. Stay with us.

He couldnt even tell who was saying it. Toju took deep breaths, or at least attempted to. His eyes kept fluttering. 

Dont close your eyes! Stay awake, damnit!

Toju couldnt help it. Before he realized it, his eyes closed and his consciousness slipped.[/spoiler]
